narr: A deluge of showers and thunderstorms continuously rocked West Virginia during the final week of July as a stationary frontal boundary remained draped over the state for a prolonged period of time. Waves of energy flowing along the front contributed to these bursts of heavy rainfall, which gradually tarnished soil conditions. Up to 5 inches of rain fell in spots south of the Interstate 64 corridor between July 26th and 27th.||Flash flooding during this time resulted in local creeks and streams rising out of their banks and spilling onto roads, primarily in Mingo, Fayette, McDowell, and Wyoming Counties. The Scarbro community in Fayette County was evacuated during the early morning hours of the 27th due to the abundance of high water impacting the township.
ev: Chestnut Grove and a nearby lumber yard flooded from backwater of Meadow River.
A bridge washed out on Russellville Road.
High water was observed along several spots within the towns of Delbarton and Red Jacket.
In the town of Hanover, high water obstructed Pad Fork Road for a brief period of time.

Local creeks in the county, including Gilbert Creek, rose above their banks and restricted access to residential homes only accessible by bridge. Several roadways within the Gilbert Creek community became washed away in spots. It would take until later that evening for roads to become accessible once again.

Nelson Branch rose out its banks and spilled onto Nelson Branch Road. Several other roads were blocked by high water for an extended amount of time between Hanover and North Spring, including Garden Gap Branch Road, North Spring Road, and Rose Branch Road. Some homes were affected.
In Isaban, water surrounded multiple homes due to Cub Creek rising out of its banks.

High water and impassable roads resulted in an evacuation of the Scarbro community. Other roads in the county became flooded and impassable during the early morning hours of the 27th, including Virginia Street, Main Street of Oak Hill, Allman Street, Scarbro Road, White Oak Fork Road, Wolf Creek Road, Shelton Road, and Summerlee Road.
